name: A Killer Game On The Screen (home switch, cages drawn, killer record only; 13 languages)
note: Written with the gate on 2026-10-01. Each mutation breaks one thing a killer player sees. Ghost and Time Gap on killer (KP-3) added 2026-10-14, Diary 130. Killer Survival (KP-2) added 2026-10-14, Diary 132: Survival opens on killer, so the "coming" note and the two mutations that broke its hand-off with the Ghost chip's note went with it.

mutations.name: killer has no Survival again
mutations.why: Replaces "a killer's Survival tab switches instead of saying it is coming" (2026-10-14, KP-2: killer has Survival, and the "coming" note went with nothing left to say it about). The killer's modes lose Survival: the tab does nothing on the killer card and the killer Survival is gone without anything else failing.
mutations.expectFailure: the Survival tab on the killer switch did not switch to Survival

mutations.name: killer has no Speedrun again
mutations.why: The killer's modes list loses Speedrun; the tab goes back to "coming soon" and the killer speedrun is gone without anything else failing.
mutations.expectFailure: did not switch to Speedrun

mutations.name: a new killer from the Speedrun tab starts as Classic
mutations.why: Home's killer button used to start Classic whatever tab was chosen. With the tab open the player sees the speedrun button and gets a classic game: no ⚡, no +10 s, hints back, the time in the wrong table.
mutations.find: const startGame = () => handleStart && handleStart(selectedLevel, false, mode, effectiveRivalMode, variant);
mutations.replace: const startGame = () => handleStart && handleStart(selectedLevel, false, 'classic', effectiveRivalMode, variant);
mutations.expectFailure: started without ⚡

mutations.name: Home's killer button drops the rival again
mutations.why: Until 2026-10-14 the killer start passed 'standard' whatever chip was chosen. The player picks Ghost, sees the record's time on the chip, and gets a new puzzle with no one to race.
mutations.find: const startGame = () => handleStart && handleStart(selectedLevel, false, mode, effectiveRivalMode, variant);
mutations.replace: const startGame = () => handleStart && handleStart(selectedLevel, false, mode, 'standard', variant);
mutations.expectFailure: no ghost banner on the killer Ghost race

mutations.name: the ⓘ shows for killer only again
mutations.why: The user's complaint: with the ⓘ on one kind only, the switch changed width when the kind changed and the layout broke. First written with the hidden attribute, which changed nothing: .rival-info-btn sets display: flex, and an author display beats the browser's [hidden] rule — it survived for that reason.
mutations.replace: <button type="button" style={{ display: variant === 'killer' ? undefined : 'none' }} className="rival-info-btn variant-rules-btn"
mutations.expectFailure: no ⓘ on the standard switch

mutations.name: the killer card drops the mode tabs
mutations.why: How the first version did it: the card lost a row on killer and jumped in height every time the kind changed. First written with the hidden attribute, which .mode-tab-group's display: grid overrides; it survived for that reason.
mutations.expectFailure: the layout jumps

mutations.name: the killer Ghost chip stays locked
mutations.why: Killer order ④ undone on the home screen: whatever killer records exist, Ghost and Time Gap never open on killer.
mutations.expectFailure: the killer Ghost chip says

mutations.name: the chips read the classic record on killer
mutations.why: The killer Ghost chip shows a classic time — a pace no killer can keep — and opens as soon as a classic level is cleared, before any killer was.
mutations.find: const ghost = getGhostForModeLevel(isTimeLimit ? 'timeAttack' : selectedMode, selectedLevel, variant);
mutations.expectFailure: the killer Ghost chip says

mutations.name: a killer Ghost race deals the record without its kind
mutations.why: The start hands the record's givens over as a classic puzzle: no cages, too few digits to have one answer, and the race is on a board that cannot be solved.
mutations.expectFailure: the killer Ghost race did not open a killer

mutations.name: a killer Ghost race reads the classic record
mutations.why: Ghost on killer replays the classic record: its board has no cages, so the race falls back to a new killer — not the board the player chose to race again.
mutations.expectFailure: not the board the record was set on

mutations.name: killer Time Gap races the classic record
mutations.why: The pace on a killer is measured against a classic time: the banner reads far behind from the first cell, and the ghost pin finishes long before any killer could.
mutations.find: const ghost = racesGhost ? getGhostForModeLevel(mode, selectedLevel, variant) : null;
mutations.replace: const ghost = racesGhost ? getGhostForModeLevel(mode, selectedLevel) : null;
mutations.expectFailure: the killer Time Gap race runs against

mutations.name: the board does not hand its cages to the win
mutations.why: The killer ghost is saved without its cages; a Ghost race cannot deal its board again and quietly deals a new one.
mutations.expectFailure: the killer ghost was saved without its cages

mutations.name: the banner counts out of a fixed 40
mutations.why: Proves the banner check reads the banner: a killer Lv.1 has 45 open cells (Lv.5 has 81), and a count out of anything else never reaches the end.
mutations.expectFailure: the player's count on the Ghost banner says

mutations.name: the ghost's count on the banner is out of a fixed 40
mutations.why: The other side of the banner: the ghost's progress out of the wrong total, so the two counts the player compares are not the same race. The first run of the player's-side mutation survived because the check read the whole banner's text and the ghost side's 0/45 matched (scope, AGENTS §3.3).
mutations.expectFailure: the ghost's count on the Ghost banner says

mutations.name: the ghost banner slides under the board
mutations.why: Proves the race's layout check measures it: the board pulled up over the banner hides the pace the player is racing.
mutations.expectFailure: .ghost-rival-banner-container and .board-zone overlap

mutations.name: a cell stops drawing the right side of its cage
mutations.why: Two cages side by side merge into one dashed shape; the player reads the wrong cells into a sum.
mutations.find: if (!right) lines.push([b, up ? 0 : a, b, down ? 100 : b]);
mutations.expectFailure: no line against the next cage

mutations.name: the sums are not drawn
mutations.why: Without the number in the corner a killer is a classic puzzle with almost no givens — unsolvable.
mutations.expectFailure: sums on the board for

mutations.name: Resume ignores the kind of the saved game
mutations.why: The standard switch offers to resume a killer, and the player lands in a killer they did not ask for.
mutations.find: const isCurrentTabSaved = hasSavedGame && (savedGame.gameMode || 'classic') === mode && variantOf(savedGame) === variant;
mutations.expectFailure: the standard switch offers to resume a killer

mutations.name: the first killer starts without its rules
mutations.why: A classic player meets dashed cages and small numbers and has nothing to say the numbers are sums.
mutations.expectFailure: the first killer started without its rules

mutations.name: a killer is graded on classic times
mutations.why: Until 2026-10-07 a killer showed no grade because the only times were classic ones, on which a killer always came out C. With killer times in speedrunRank.js, the victory screen must pass the kind; without it a killer in 105 s at Lv.1 reads A instead of S+.
mutations.find: const rankInfo = speedrunRankFor(level, gameMode, actualSeconds, variant, playedSeconds);
mutations.replace: const rankInfo = speedrunRankFor(level, gameMode, actualSeconds, 'classic', playedSeconds);
mutations.expectFailure: graded on classic times, not the killer ones

mutations.name: the switch's names are set too large to fit
mutations.why: Proves the 13-language sweep measures the switch: at this size the longer names no longer fit their half.
mutations.expectFailure: switch —

mutations.name: the rules lines do not wrap
mutations.why: Proves the sweep measures the rules card: an unwrapped rule widens the card past the screen in every language. First written without !important, and it changed nothing — `text-wrap: pretty` further down the same rule sets the wrap mode back (both are shorthands for text-wrap-mode, the later one wins) — so it survived for that reason, not for a gap in the gate.
mutations.expectFailure: rules —

mutations.name: a killer win hides the leaderboard again
mutations.why: Until 2026-10-08 the victory screen dropped the leaderboard button for a killer, whose wins did not reach the Logic Score. They do now; hiding it leaves a killer player no way to the board their win just moved.
mutations.expectFailure: a killer win offers no leaderboard

mutations.name: the Ghost chip in Survival gives the "clear this level" reason
mutations.why: In Survival Ghost and Time Gap are off by design; telling the player to go and earn them sends them after something that never comes (user report, 2026-09-26) — now on the killer card too.
mutations.expectFailure: the Ghost chip in killer Survival says

mutations.name: a new game takes the limit of the kind played before
mutations.why: Added 2026-10-14 (KP-2). The new kind is set in state for the next render, so the clock read it too early: a killer Survival started after a classic game (or on a fresh launch) gets the classic 4 minutes.
mutations.expectFailure: started with

mutations.name: a killer is paid the classic 7 s a cell
mutations.why: The killer bonus (9 s at Lv.1) is what keeps a killer Survival as tight as a classic one; at 7 s it runs out sooner on every level.
mutations.expectFailure: a right cell moved the killer Survival clock

mutations.name: a killer lost on time counts against the classic record
mutations.why: The clock running out on a killer lowers the classic win rate — the Logic Score's accuracy — and the killer card never shows the loss.
mutations.expectFailure: a killer Survival lost on time left

mutations.name: a killer Survival is graded on the time left
mutations.why: Without the seconds played the victory screen grades the clock — in Survival the time left (D15) — so a fast clear with time to spare reads as the slowest grade.
mutations.find: const rankInfo = speedrunRankFor(level, gameMode, actualSeconds, variant, playedSeconds);
mutations.replace: const rankInfo = speedrunRankFor(level, gameMode, actualSeconds, variant);
mutations.expectFailure: expected S+ on the killer times, by the seconds played

mutations.name: the killer card's Survival rows read the plain best times
mutations.why: The Survival block on the killer card shows the wrong table: a killer Survival clear never appears, and a plain killer time sits under the hourglass.
mutations.expectFailure: the killer card's Survival Lv.1 says

mutations.name: the AI lobby starts the match without the kind picked
mutations.why: The switch moves and nothing follows it: Killer picked in the AI lobby, a classic dealt.
mutations.expectFailure: Killer in the AI lobby dealt a classic room

mutations.name: the router drops the kind on its way to the AI room
mutations.why: Same promise broken one step later: the lobby names the kind and the router starts the match without it.
mutations.expectFailure: Killer in the AI lobby dealt a classic room

mutations.name: the first AI match deals only the board and the solution
mutations.why: The hand-off before KP-11: the room is a killer and the game is a classic on its givens — no cages drawn, mistakes not told about cages.
mutations.expectFailure: the killer AI battle board is not a killer board

mutations.name: a rematch after a killer is a classic
mutations.why: The player asks for the same match again and gets the other kind — as solo follow-ups did before gate 3-19.
mutations.expectFailure: the rematch after a killer AI battle is a classic

mutations.name: a rematch deals only the board and the solution
mutations.why: The rematch room is a killer and the board drawn is not: no outlines, no sums.
mutations.expectFailure: rematch outline

mutations.name: the first killer AI battle starts without its rules
mutations.why: A player who has only played standard sudoku meets dashed cages and small numbers against a running bot, with no way to guess the numbers are sums.
mutations.expectFailure: the first killer AI battle started without its rules

mutations.name: the rules card in the AI lobby only closes
mutations.why: The player reads the rules, taps Start and is back in the lobby: the first killer match never begins.
mutations.expectFailure: the rules card did not start the AI battle

mutations.name: the AI lobby keeps a kind of its own
mutations.why: Two answers to "which kind am I playing": Killer in the lobby, standard on Home (user, 2026-10-14: one remembered choice).
mutations.expectFailure: Killer was picked in the AI lobby and Home shows standard

mutations.name: a killer duel lost on mistakes counts as a killer played
mutations.why: BT-1, on the screen: the duel record already counts the loss, and counting it in the killer record too lowers the killer win rate for a match the win path never counts.
mutations.expectFailure: a killer AI battle lost on mistakes counted

mutations.name: the AI lobby switch runs off the screen
mutations.why: Proves section 6 measures the switch in the AI lobby and not only on Home: pushed past the edge there, every language must say so.
mutations.expectFailure: AI lobby switch —
